political_impact.text: The order gave the Navy one official form for naming its vessels: the ship's name preceded by "United States Ship" or "U.S.S." and nothing else, replacing a mix of forms by type, rig or function.
political_impact.source: Executive Order 549; Naval Historical Center, "USN Ship Naming" (1997)

legacy.text: The Naval History and Heritage Command credits this order with establishing the present usage, and the "USS" before every commissioned American warship traces to it.
legacy.source: Naval History and Heritage Command, account of ship naming

today.name: "USS" ship prefix of the U.S. Navy
today.note: The Navy cites EO 549 as the order that established the present usage.

political_impact.text: The Governor of Tutuila could now issue certificates of protection that served as ship's papers for Samoan-owned vessels that could not be documented as United States vessels.

related.note: The same order filed under a second number; the 1944 catalog marks EO 548 identical with EO 546.

legacy.text: The certificates concerned ships, not persons; people born in American Samoa remain U.S. nationals but not citizens, a status courts upheld in Tuaua (2015) and Fitisemanu (2021).
legacy.source: 8 U.S.C. §§ 1101(a)(29), 1408; Tuaua v. United States, 788 F.3d 300 (D.C. Cir. 2015); Fitisemanu v. United States (10th Cir. 2021)

related.note: Identical order carried under a second number.

political_impact.text: Coal-withdrawn land inside the new forest-reserve boundaries went into the reserves while the coal withdrawals stayed in force, so both rules applied to the same ground.

legacy.text: The order fed into the larger mineral-withdrawal program that Congress later ratified in the Pickett Act of 1910 and the Mineral Leasing Act of 1920.

later_actions.text: The Pickett Act was one of the laws by which Congress ratified the mineral-withdrawal program this order belonged to.
The Mineral Leasing Act completed Congress's ratification of the mineral-withdrawal program.

uncertain: The operative text of Executive Order 576 has not been found in any published source; only its catalog title is known.

today.name: San Juan Islands National Wildlife Refuge
today.note: Viti Rocks, off the south end of Lummi Island, are now part of the refuge.

reception.text: The Washington Evening Star reported the President's instruction excusing Grand Army members for the Alger funeral on the day it was given.

political_impact.text: Alger's funeral was held at his Washington home on January 26, and the Senate adjourned to attend.

related.note: EO 574 amended the Hot Springs hospital regulations again and commuted the ration at thirty cents.
Further amended the Hot Springs hospital rations and subsistence rules.

political_impact.text: None of these orders was national news; the issues of early 1907 that reached the newspapers were the forest-reserve fight and the Japanese immigration crisis.
